Directions: Read the passage about Bill Bowerman, the inventor of the waffle tread running shoe. Then answer the questions that follow.
Title: Finding Inspiration
Author: by Laurie Lawlor
Content: Inspiration sometimes comes at random times. For example, Bill Bowerman (`1911-1999`) came up with an idea for a running shoe after looking more closely at his family's waffle iron.

Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, Bowerman was a devoted teacher with a passion for running. He believed that running offered a great way for individuals to improve their physical health. He promoted jogging to people of all ages. He even wrote a popular book about the subject in `1967`.

From `1948` to `1972`, Bowerman guided an impressive list of track-and-field champions at the University of Oregon. He also coached the `1972` U.S. Olympic track-and-field team. “Victory,” Bowerman reminded his runners, “is doing the best you can, and even if you lose, you will have learned something.”

Throughout his life, Bowerman looked for practical solutions to problems. He helped develop rubberized asphalt runways that proved safer than grass in rainy weather for track-and-field events. But it was his contributions to running shoes that really changed the sport.

Bowerman believed that the spiked running shoes worn in the `text(1950s)` were clumsy and heavy. They also caused injuries. “Poorly designed shoes,” he said, “... caused more shin splints, foot sores, leg cramps and aching knees and backs than anything else.” He believed a lighter, more flexible shoe was possible.

Bowerman spent `text(years)` tinkering with shoe designs. He began by making individual, lightweight shoes for each of his athletes. He introduced the arch support and the cushioned midsole. When he couldn't find a company to make his shoes, he and a former student, Phil Knight, teamed up...

And the waffle iron's role in all this? Watching waffles being made `text(one)` morning made Bowerman wonder if a similar pattern on the soles of running shoes might create better traction. Bowerman's “waffle” tread idea — which resulted after he poured liquid urethane onto the waffle iron — changed the industry.

In `1971`, Bowerman and Knight launched [their own] brand... At the `1972` Munich Olympics, `text(four)` of the top `text(seven)` finishers in the marathon event wore the now-famous ... running shoes. Further improvements to the shoe's weight came when Bowerman switched the traditional upper shoe material to lighter nylon.
In `1980`, Bowerman and Knight ... began selling running shoes to professionals and recreational runners in more than `100` countries around the world.
